cues.text: This is smooth ribbon seagrass, Cymodocea rotundata.
What you are seeing is a display, not a scan of a meadow in Mati.
There are no teeth along the edge.
On the short stem, the sheath scars join into a closed ring.
That ring is how you tell this plant from serrated ribbon seagrass, which does not close its scars.
The patch spreads when the buried stem grows through the sand and sends up new shoots.
Roots grow down at each node.
The plant can also flower and set seed.
